head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Dan Koh
text: Told ABC News he supports Jeffries for Speaker.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Ted Lieu
text: Caucus vice chair who called Jeffries an amazing leader and says Democrats will elect him Speaker.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Pete Aguilar
text: Says the outcome of the Speaker race is not in question, backing Jeffries.

head: News: Vice chair is the only contested House leadership race
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: ABC News reports Jeffries is expected to win the caucus vote with no challenger, while Lauren Underwood and Sara Jacobs contest vice chair.

head: News: Speaker nominee picked by secret ballot, only total released
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: TIME reports that members vote on House-issued phones by secret ballot. The overall tally will be published but not how each member voted.

head: Reported: Some incoming progressives yet to commit to Jeffries
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: CBS News reports that some incoming progressives have not committed and want to weigh their options or hear his policy positions first. No member is named.

head: Reported: Leonard met Jeffries after 'living hell' warning
name: Don Leonard
text: TIME reports that Leonard, who said senior Democrats warned him over refusing to back Jeffries, has since met him. His position after the meeting is not clear.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Emily Randall
text: Told AP she is supporting Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker and expects him to win.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Shomari Figures
text: Told AP he will stand by Jeffries in the caucus vote for Speaker.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
text: Told reporters at the Capitol that Jeffries is the only candidate in the Speaker race, restating her support.

head: News: Jeffries unopposed as caucus votes on Speaker nominee
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: House Democrats meet privately on 18 November to nominate a Speaker. Jeffries is running unopposed and has asked for a recorded vote, with the floor vote on 3 January.

head: On record: Ansari praises Jeffries as a collaborative leader
name: Yassamin Ansari
text: Ansari told AP that Jeffries is a collaborative leader whose job is to reflect the whole caucus, not one faction. She did not state a formal endorsement in the report.

head: News: Van Hollen claims 15 votes, Schumer says he has the votes
name: Chris Van Hollen
text: The Hill reports Van Hollen says he has 15 votes, while only four voting Democrats have publicly backed him. Schumer told reporters he has the votes.

head: Undecided
name: Ben Ray Luján
text: Declined to say who he backs and wants commitments from both candidates. Wants the vote kept in December.

head: Undecided
name: Martin Heinrich
text: Still not saying who he backs. Wants to hear from the incoming freshman senators first.

head: News: Senate Democrats keep leader vote on 1 December
name: Chuck Schumer
text: Senate Democrats pushed back on talk of an earlier leadership vote and plan to hold it on 1 December, most likely by secret ballot. Roll Call puts the winning number at 29 if Peltola holds her Alaska lead.

head: On record: Jeffries says the caucus will work its will
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: On the eve of the caucus vote, Jeffries said he was talking with members across the caucus. CBS New York reported he wants members to record their votes.

head: On record: Schumer says "I have the votes" to stay leader
name: Chuck Schumer
text: Schumer told CBS New York he is confident he will be the next leader and has the votes, despite Van Hollen's challenge. The vote is set for 1 December.

head: News: Jeffries has no declared rival in caucus speaker vote
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: AFP reports Jeffries faces no declared challenger in Wednesday's closed-door caucus vote, though some new progressives are withholding support. The formal floor vote is on 3 January.

head: On record: Schumer says his focus is on 2027, not 2028
name: Chuck Schumer
text: Schumer told Punchbowl News his total focus is on 2027 and declined to discuss whether he will run again in 2028. Punchbowl also reported he says he has the votes to stay leader.

head: On record: Murray points to caucus discussion, no pick yet
name: Patty Murray
text: Murray told The Hill she expects a great caucus discussion and has not said how she will vote. The Hill reported Schumer allies expect her to back him.

head: On record: Jeffries says he takes nothing for granted
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: Ahead of the caucus vote, Jeffries said he is in a great place but takes nothing for granted. He has asked for a tallied secret-ballot vote rather than acclamation.

head: News: Jeffries courts progressives before caucus vote
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: Newsweek reported Jeffries is reaching out to progressives before the 18 November caucus vote. No Democrat has formally challenged him, though a petition urges Ayanna Pressley to run.

head: Leaning Schumer
name: Tim Kaine
text: Defended Schumer after the election win, but AP reports he is still open to Van Hollen or another candidate.

head: Undecided
name: Jon Ossoff
text: Says he has not committed to Schumer or Van Hollen and wants to hear each candidate's vision.

head: Undecided
name: Josh Turek
text: Has met both Schumer and Van Hollen and wants more specifics, including on anti-corruption, before deciding.

head: On record: Andrews in talks with both leader candidates
name: Annie Andrews
text: Andrews said on Tuesday she is in conversations with both Schumer and Van Hollen. She did not say how she will vote.

head: On record: Hickenlooper still won't say how he'll vote
name: John Hickenlooper
text: Asked how he would vote, Hickenlooper replied "Leave it to the Democrats" and did not commit.

head: On record: Slotkin declines to name her pick
name: Elissa Slotkin
text: Slotkin told reporters she is not saying anything about the race. AP notes she has not endorsed Van Hollen.

head: Reported: Warren declines to say who she backs
name: Elizabeth Warren
text: AP reports Warren declined to say whether she supports Schumer or Van Hollen.

head: News: AP counts about 15 senators publicly for Schumer
name: Chuck Schumer
text: An AP count finds about 15 incoming Democratic senators publicly backing Schumer and four backing Van Hollen. Schumer says he is confident he has the votes.

head: News: Jeffries opts for a recorded caucus vote, not acclamation
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: Jeffries confirmed his nomination will go to a vote in Wednesday's closed-door caucus meeting rather than being approved by acclamation. No challenger has been named.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Chris Van Hollen
text: Challenging Schumer. Now says he has locked down 15 votes, though only four colleagues back him publicly.

head: News: Van Hollen says backers fear Schumer retaliation
name: Chris Van Hollen
text: Van Hollen said some senators backing him are staying quiet for fear of retaliation from Schumer, and disputed that Schumer has the race locked up. The secret ballot is set for 1 December.

head: On record: Alsobrooks declines to take a position
name: Angela Alsobrooks
text: Asked about the leader race, Alsobrooks declined to take a position and said a big discussion was coming. She was earlier reported as backing Schumer.

head: On record: Ossoff opposes bringing the leader vote forward
name: Jon Ossoff
text: Ossoff said he would oppose expediting the leadership vote before a full process. He has not said who he backs.

head: On record: Coons calls Van Hollen's chances remote
name: Chris Coons
text: Coons praised the party's midterm results and described Van Hollen's chances as remote. He has not formally endorsed either candidate.

head: On record: Pressley dismisses a challenge to Jeffries
name: Ayanna Pressley
text: At a town hall on Monday, Pressley rejected calls to run, saying she does not need to be Speaker to speak for the people.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Mazie Hirono
text: Backs Schumer for leader, citing her long history with him, while praising Van Hollen.

head: Undecided
name: John Hickenlooper
text: Publicly undecided. Credits Schumer for the Senate gains but says it is healthy to review how the caucus works.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Richard Blumenthal
text: Listed by The Hill's whip count as publicly backing Schumer, resolving earlier conflicting reports.

head: Senator backs Jeffries
name: Chris Van Hollen
text: Van Hollen, who is challenging Schumer for Senate leader, told POLITICO he supports Jeffries for Speaker and that Jeffries should get the chance to bring the caucus together. As a senator, he has no vote in the House.

head: Leaning against Jeffries
name: Don Leonard
text: Set out red lines on campaign finance and Israel aid before he'll vote for Jeffries.

head: News: Hardy concedes NC-7 to Rouzer, seat stays Republican
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: Democrat Kimberly Hardy conceded the North Carolina 7th District race to Republican David Rouzer, saying a recount could not close the gap of about 2,300 votes.

head: Undecided
name: Scott Colom
text: Told CNN and NBC on 15 Nov he's still listening and doesn't know either candidate well. No pick yet.

head: Undecided
name: Jake Johnson
text: Told the Minnesota Star Tribune he hasn't committed on speaker and wants to see his options first.

head: Opposed to Schumer
name: Annie Andrews
text: The Post and Courier reports she has already said she would not back Schumer for leader. That is a public refusal rather than a lean, though she has not named Van Hollen.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: John Fetterman
text: Newer evidence, no change in stance. Speaking to Fox News at the weekend, he said a Van Hollen win would trouble him, reaffirming his backing for Schumer.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Kirsten Gillibrand
text: Praised Schumer's strategic leadership and backs him.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Ruben Gallego
text: Compared Schumer to a manager who earns a new contract after a winning season.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Sherrod Brown
text: Only incoming senator to say he'll back Schumer; says Schumer knows how to govern.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Chris Van Hollen
text: Challenging Schumer. Says he has more than 10 senators privately behind him.

head: Opposed to Schumer
name: Adam Hamilton
text: Said publicly he won't vote for Schumer. Hasn't named an alternative.

head: Leaning against Schumer
name: Juliana Stratton
text: Has said she would oppose Schumer, though some reports say she avoids a clear stance.

head: Leaning against Schumer
name: Annie Andrews
text: Wants generational change and has said she'd oppose Schumer.

head: Undecided
name: Raphael Warnock
text: Won't commit. Says Democrats are at an inflection point.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
text: Asked whether she backs Jeffries, said yes, noting the race is unopposed.

head: Leaning Jeffries
name: Pramila Jayapal
text: Reports conflict. Some outlets list her as backing Jeffries; Al Jazeera reports she's withholding support pending a Medicare for All commitment.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Mark Kelly
text: Backs Schumer while calling for a new plan.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Jack Reed
text: Official statement saying he will support Schumer.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Peggy Flanagan
text: Endorsed Van Hollen on X after saying it's time for new leadership.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Jeff Merkley
text: Endorsed Van Hollen on X.

head: Opposed to Schumer
name: Elissa Slotkin
text: Said she won't back Schumer and floated withholding a quorum until he presents a plan.

head: Undecided
name: James Talarico
text: Hasn't committed. Wants to hear Schumer's vision for the Senate first.

head: Undecided
name: Chris Coons
text: Says he's open to hearing other candidates.

head: Undecided
name: Andy Kim
text: Uncommitted. Wants a caucus discussion first.

head: Undecided
name: Cory Booker
text: Wants a family conversation within the caucus. Hasn't committed.

head: Undecided
name: Adelita Grijalva
text: Wouldn't say whether she plans to vote for Jeffries.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Angus King
text: Restated support for Schumer in a statement after Van Hollen launched his bid.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Tammy Baldwin
text: Official statement saying she will support Schumer.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Catherine Cortez Masto
text: Reaffirmed support for Schumer after Van Hollen announced his run.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Jacky Rosen
text: Endorsed Schumer after Van Hollen entered the race.

head: Leaning Schumer
name: Richard Blumenthal
text: Reports conflict. Said he plans to back Schumer, but a later list has him refusing to commit.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Bernie Sanders
text: Won't back Schumer and endorsed Van Hollen's bid.

head: Backs Van Hollen
name: Abdul El-Sayed
text: Endorsed Van Hollen the night he announced. Schumer backed his primary opponent.

head: Undecided
name: Chris Pappas
text: Has called for a new generation of leadership but hasn't committed.

head: Undecided
name: Patty Murray
text: Didn't commit either way. Says the caucus will decide.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: John Fetterman
text: Said he will vote for Schumer.

head: Undecided
name: Mark Warner
text: Praised Schumer's fundraising but won't commit.

head: Undecided
name: Peter Welch
text: Left the choice open while saying he's committed to change.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Chuck Schumer
text: Running for another term as leader and says he has the votes.

head: Undecided
name: Michael Bennet
text: Hasn't committed.

head: Undecided
name: Martin Heinrich
text: Not committing.

head: Undecided
name: Alex Padilla
text: Noncommittal before a caucus lunch.

head: Leaning Jeffries
name: Brad Schneider
text: Called Jeffries 'our leader' in a February New Democrat Coalition statement. The coalition endorsed his speaker bid this month.

head: Leaning Jeffries
name: William Lawrence
text: Latest report has him backing Jeffries. Earlier coverage listed him as leaning against.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Brian Schatz
text: Publicly supported Schumer; expected to be the next whip.

head: Opposed to Schumer
name: Troy Jackson
text: Told Schumer he'll support somebody else, but won't back Van Hollen just because he's the alternative.

head: Undecided
name: Josh Turek
text: Declined to affirm support for Schumer. One report expected him to back Schumer.

head: Opposed to Jeffries
name: Angela Gonzales-Torres
text: Says her vote is no as of now.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Sheldon Whitehouse
text: Said the election result justifies another Schumer term.

head: Undecided
name: Ed Markey
text: Declined to endorse Schumer.

head: Leaning Jeffries
name: Jim Himes
text: Has said Jeffries will be speaker. A prediction rather than a pledge.

head: Undecided
name: Jon Ossoff
text: His campaign wouldn't say whether he'd back Schumer.

head: Undecided
name: Maria Cantwell
text: Credited Schumer for the win but says she'll listen to the debate.

head: Declared for Jeffries
name: Hakeem Jeffries
text: Running for Speaker. Formally launched his bid in a letter to colleagues.

head: Declared for Schumer
name: Angela Alsobrooks
text: Publicly backed Schumer before her state colleague Van Hollen entered the race.

head: Undecided
name: Ben Ray Luján
text: No pledge found. Asked who was running against Schumer.
